Let's knit this gorgeous baby blanket
featuring delicate angels and hearts.
I'll show you exactly how!
I'm going to show you step-by-step exactly how to

make this sweet treasure of a baby
blanket.  By the end of this video you'll

know exactly what skill level this
project requires, the yarn and supplies

you need to complete it, how to make
beautiful sample swatches, where to

purchase the pattern, and free bonus how
to make a blanket out of the sample swatches.
This is an advanced easy project using the thread lace technique.

It's easy because if you know how to
cast on, knit and purl stockinette plus bind

off, that's the total physical skill
level necessary.  The challenge becomes
working with two yarns held together, one a sport weight the other a fingering yarn

working most stitches holding both yarns
together and knitting only the fingering

yarn where designated.  This is what
creates the delicate lacy look.  This is a

30 inch long blanket and that means a
lot of stitches on the needles and

dozens of rows.  It also means learning to
read fol; graphs as well as written

instructions to make it successfully.
You'll learn how to duplicate stitch the

heart on to the angel. This tutorial
demonstrating exactly how to knit the

angel and heart swatches sets you are
perfectly to master the actual blanket.

Plus as promised, we'll talk about
alternatively simply making several

small swatches and just crocheting them
together in patchwork to make any size

blanket you desire.  ow if you're more
interested in making a baby blanket with

dragonflies or butterflies, click the i
in the upper right hand corner or click

the link in the description below, and
machine knitters catch the link in the

description below to all of these same
patterns adapted to the Brother bulky

knitting machine.  Okay, on to our angels
project.  You are going to need Loops and
Thread Snuggly-Wuggly baby support yarn or

Lion Brand Pound of Love is great - Tamm
Estilo cone fingering yarn, scissors, size

8 or 5 mm knitting needles and
size H or 5 mm crochet hook.
You can get all of these items at your local craft store except the cone yarn or

online and I've placed links in the
description below for how to get that
cone yarn.  Now the cone yarn does cost a bit, however. it would make at least five

of these blankets and probably more so
that it ends up costing you no more

per blanket really than the baby sport
costs.  Think about sharing the cone yarn

with your knitting group and the bunch of
you could get cracking on these thread

lace blankets and have a wonderful time
knitting for a cause.  Now that you know

the supplies list, want to make something
faster than a blanket with these angels?

Make a dog sweater instead and you can
find the link to that pattern in hand
knitting in the description below.

Hey knitters!  If you enjoyed this video
let me know it by hitting the like

button below and as long as you're down

in the description below and make

yourself a sweet confection of a glad

summary.brief: A woman demonstrates how to knit an Angels & Hearts baby blanket, shows the needed supplies and finished pieces, and ends with a dog wearing the knitted sweater.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a close‑up of a woman wearing glasses, red lipstick and a ring, sitting with a young child who is holding an unfinished pink blanket embroidered with blue and white hearts. She greets the child and introduces the Angels & Hearts baby blanket tutorial. The camera then shifts to a white background where she displays the pink sport‑weight yarn, the white fingering yarn, a pair of gold knitting needles, scissors and a crochet hook. She begins a close‑up, sped‑up demonstration of knitting: holding the two yarns together on the needles, inserting the right needle into the stitches on the left needle, wrapping the yarn and pulling it through to form stockinette stitches, repeating row after row to build the lace‑like blanket. Interleaved shots show a baby lying in a bassinet wrapped in the partially finished blanket, and later the completed blanket alongside other finished swatches and the tools. The segment concludes with a shot of a dog wearing a pink sweater, followed by an “End of Part 1” title screen and YouTube subscribe graphics.

action.detailed: Using two gold knitting needles, she holds the pink sport yarn and white fingering yarn together, inserts the right needle into the stitches on the left needle, wraps the yarn around the right needle, pulls it through to create a new stitch, and repeats across the row to build the lace‑style blanket.

llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to any of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   - "navigation": the camera moves through a physical environment as an
     agent traverses space — first-person walking tours (museum, store,
     home, city street), driving / cycling / hiking POV footage, drone
     fly-throughs of indoor or outdoor scenes, room/house walkthroughs.
     The camera's translation through the environment IS the main content.
     Does NOT count: a stationary tripod with someone talking; a tutorial
     filmed in one place; b-roll where the camera only pans or zooms but
     does not translate; sports footage where the player moves but the
     camera stays put.
   A video can match zero, one, or multiple domains. Be strict — when in
   doubt, say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
